claims.text: The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy contains microscale compositional fluctuations.
Compositional fluctuations create microregions with different thermal-expansion coefficients.
Compositional fluctuations produce local regions with differing lattice parameters.
Thermal-expansion mismatch between microregions generates localized residual stresses during thermal cycling.
Mismatch-induced residual stresses alter dislocation mobility.
Mismatch-induced residual stresses act as dislocation-pinning points during deformation.
Mismatch-induced residual stresses shift the alloy's elastic moduli.
The proposed mismatch-stress mechanism explains the alloy's high-temperature creep behavior.
The proposed mismatch-stress mechanism explains microhardness variations after cold rolling.
The proposed mismatch-stress mechanism explains changes in elastic properties over the investigated temperature range.
Prolonged high-temperature annealing will homogenize the composition and reduce thermal-expansion mismatch between microregions.
The homogenized alloy will have lower residual or internal stresses than the as-cast alloy.
The homogenized alloy will exhibit more uniform lattice parameters than the as-cast alloy.
The homogenized alloy will have a lower tensile-creep rate at 1250 °C than the as-cast alloy.
The homogenized alloy will show diminished work hardening and smaller microhardness changes during cold rolling.
The homogenized alloy will show a more conventional temperature dependence of elastic moduli.
The magnitude of the thermal-expansion-mismatch effect depends on the length scales and spatial distribution of compositional heterogeneities.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says mismatch stresses pin dislocations, which ordinarily implies impeded dislocation motion, but the predicted outcome says removing those stresses will lower the creep rate. No additional step explains why removing the proposed pinning would improve creep resistance.
